description: This bar chart, from the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models,” illustrates the average effect sizes for six different multilingual transformer models—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across nine linguistic categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The horizontal axis lists these linguistic categories in order from left to right, while the vertical axis, labeled “effect,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each linguistic category is represented by a group of six colored bars, corresponding to the six models as defined in the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). Error bars are present for each bar, indicating the standard deviation or uncertainty in the measured effect. The bars are not sorted by value; they appear in the order of the linguistic categories as listed. Visually, the IE-Indic category shows the highest overall effect, with mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ bars reaching approximately 15–16, while the IE-Baltic category shows the lowest effects, with all bars below 5. The Semitic category also shows relatively high effects, particularly for XLM-B₂ and XLM-L₂, which reach approximately 15 and 13 respectively. The Isolate category shows very low effects across all models, with values near or below 1. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlines beyond their inherent color coding.
